title: A binding-to-release strategy for targeted anticancer drug delivery.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC core record (isOpenAccess=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no PMCID, only 'Subscription required' full-text link); Europe PMC datalinks endpoint = 0 hits; no accessions anywhere in the retrievable text; Zenodo searched for the DOI stem and for 'PhoPEx' = 0 records; Figshare search endpoint returned 404; RCSB Protein Data Bank search on this paper's DOI returned no deposited structures; the publisher page redirected to a login gateway (idp.nature.com), so no Data Availability statement could be read.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything scientific: the abstract alone. The binding-to-release (BTR) concept, the phosphorus(V)-phenol exchange (PhoPEx) chemistry, the fibroblast activation protein (FAP) and PD-L1 (programmed cell death ligand 1) conjugates, and all quantitative claims (5.9-fold higher monomethyl auristatin E exposure in tumours, 14.7-fold tumour-to-blood ratio, 55.1-fold tumour-to-liver ratio) are abstract claims I could not check against any file.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified not from the paper text but from the repositories: the article is subscription-only with no PubMed Central copy, Europe PMC reports no supplementary files and no data links, and searches of Zenodo, Figshare and the Protein Data Bank on the paper's DOI returned nothing. There is no dataset to download, and the publisher page requires a login.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Cannot be checked, and would almost certainly fail. Any prediction target here (payload release rate, tumour-to-blood ratio) exists only as numbers inside figures and spectra in the paywalled supplementary information, so it would have to be constructed by hand from figure panels.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not verifiable. Conjugate structures would be drawn in schemes, not provided as SMILES (a text format for chemical structures), so every input molecule would have to be redrawn by hand.

a4_units_stated.note: Not verifiable without the files. Units for the headline numbers (AUC in hours times concentration, fold-ratios) are stated in the abstract but no tabular data exists to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL on the paper's own design. This is a single-platform wet-lab chemistry and pharmacology study: a handful of synthesised conjugates against two targets (FAP and PD-L1) in mouse tumour models and a small set of patient lymph nodes. That is tens of measurements, not the ~1,500 labelled rows the checklist requires. No row count verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: under 0.1 GB if any table existed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized, but only because there is essentially no data.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable: there is no download to compare against the paper, and no API record of any deposited dataset.

a8_label_provenance.note: The underlying measurements (drug concentration in tissue by mass spectrometry, tumour volume, staining intensity) are genuine physical measurements, not another model's output. This is the one Part A item that is not a problem.

existing_models.name: BIreactive (2020 model that estimates how reactive a covalent drug's reactive group, or 'warhead', is, by learning from quantum-chemistry activation energies)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; I saw only the journal listing (Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling, 2020), not the reported numbers or split.

existing_models.name: ADCNet, DumplingGNN and Linker-GPT (models for antibody-drug conjugate activity, payload toxicity and linker stability, named in a 2025 npj Precision Oncology review)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; named only inside a review's summary, so I have no numbers or splits for them.

backbone.name: ChemBERTa (a language model pretrained on chemical structures written as SMILES text)
backbone.hardware: CPU only would suffice, but there is no labelled table to fit a head on.
backbone.licence: ChemBERTa is permissively licensed; irrelevant here because the data does not exist.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. ChEMBL (a large public database of compound bioactivities) would be the natural partner for release-rate or potency data, but this paper provides no chemical identifiers to join on.
integration.join_key: none present (no SMILES, InChIKey, UniProt accession or any other identifier retrievable)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: with no machine-readable structures or measurements released, there is nothing to join.

controls.positive_control: None available. The paper's own internalization-dependent conjugate (FAP-ITR-SMDC) would be the obvious comparator, but its measurements are not released as data.
controls.external_validation: None. No second dataset measures payload release from binding-to-release conjugates, because the chemistry is new to this paper.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is possible: with no released data, any model built from this paper would be trained on numbers transcribed by eye from figures in a paywalled supplement.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use conjugate chemical structure and target pocket context to predict how fast a bound drug payload is released.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered was: for each drug conjugate, its chemical structure plus a description of the nucleophilic (electron-donating, reactive) amino acid near the binding pocket of its protein target. Number of examples: unknown, and almost certainly only tens.
plain_idea.predict: The payload release rate or the resulting tumour-to-blood drug ratio, measured by mass spectrometry of drug concentrations in mouse tissue. Those measurements exist only inside the paper's figures.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Medicinal chemistry groups building drug conjugates for poorly internalizing targets would want to know, before synthesis, which electrophile-and-pocket pairings release payload efficiently. Nothing is learnable here, though, because the measurements were never deposited.

more_or_better_data.why: There is no accessible data at all: Europe PMC reports no supplementary files and no data links, and Zenodo, Figshare and the Protein Data Bank have nothing under this DOI.

confidence_score.why: Per-prediction confidence needs replicate measurements in a machine-readable table; none were released.

models_beatable.why: BIreactive (2020) is old and closed, which would normally be an opening, but I could not retrieve its numbers and we have no training data to beat it with.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: no existing model can be run as a baseline on this paper's data, because this paper has no downloadable data.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict payload release efficiency (or tumour-to-blood drug ratio) for binding-to-release drug conjugates from the conjugate's chemical structure plus the identity and geometry of the nucleophilic residue in the target's binding pocket. The idea is scientifically appealing and likely under-modelled, but this paper supplies no machine-readable structures and no measurement table, so it cannot be built from this source.

effort.compute_note: No estimates made: there is no dataset to size. Compute was never the constraint.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Query Europe PMC for supplementary files and data links on the PubMed ID, then search Zenodo, Figshare and the Protein Data Bank on the DOI. All four returned nothing in under two minutes, which killed the candidate.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright: the Nature article is subscription-only with no PubMed Central copy, Europe PMC reports zero supplementary files and zero data links, and Zenodo, Figshare and the Protein Data Bank hold nothing under this DOI, so no file can be opened. A5 fails as well by the study's own design, since a new bioconjugation chemistry demonstrated on two targets in mouse models and a few patient lymph nodes yields tens of measurements, not the ~1,500 labelled rows needed. Excellent chemistry, no dataset.
